questions.question: How to read |一日| in: 来月の一日に会いましょう?
questions.explanation: 一日 has TWO readings: ついたち (the 1st of the month) vs いちにち (one day, a duration). Here it's a date → ついたち. Compare: 一日中 = いちにちじゅう (all day long).

questions.question: How to read |一日| in: 一日中、本を読みました?
questions.explanation: Here 一日 means 'one whole day' (duration), so いちにち. The trap: ついたち only works for the calendar 1st.

questions.question: How to read |二十日| in: 三月の二十日に来ます?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 二十日 (the 20th) is irregularly read はつか. NOT にじゅうにち. This is one of the most tested date readings in N5.

questions.question: How to read |八日| (the 8th of the month)?
questions.explanation: 8日 = ようか. Pattern of irregular date readings: 4日 よっか, 8日 ようか, 20日 はつか — these three are most commonly confused.

questions.question: How to read |四日| (the 4th of the month)?
questions.explanation: 4日 = よっか. Note: 14日 = じゅうよっか, 24日 = にじゅうよっか follow the same pattern.

questions.question: How to read |十日| (the 10th of the month)?
questions.explanation: 10日 = とおか, using the kun-yomi とお of 十. Days 1-10 mostly use kun-yomi readings (ついたち, ふつか, みっか...).

questions.question: How to read |九日| (the 9th of the month)?
questions.explanation: 9日 = ここのか. Compare with 9時 = くじ — different counters use different number readings.

questions.question: How to read |二人| in: 兄弟は二人います?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 1人 ひとり and 2人 ふたり are the only 'irregular' people-counter readings. From 3人 onwards, use にん: 三人 さんにん, 四人 よにん, etc.

questions.question: How to read |四人| in: テーブルに四人座っています?
questions.explanation: 4人 = よにん. NOT よんにん in standard Japanese. NOT しにん (which sounds like 死人 = dead person — avoided).

questions.question: How to read |七人|?
questions.explanation: 7人 can be read しちにん (more traditional) or ななにん (modern, clearer). Both appear in JLPT materials. しちにん is slightly more standard in formal contexts.

questions.question: How to read |何人| in: クラスに何人いますか?
questions.explanation: 何人 (なんにん) = how many people. ⚠ Trap: なんじん also exists but means 'people of what nationality?' (e.g., あの人は何人ですか — what nationality is that person?).

questions.question: How to read |一月| in: 一月に日本へ来ました?
questions.explanation: Here 一月 means 'January' (the month name), so いちがつ. Different reading 一月 (ひとつき) means 'one month duration' — that's a separate, less common usage.

questions.question: How to read |四月|?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 4月 = しがつ. Even though 4 is usually よん/よ in Japanese, all month names use the on-yomi consistently: 4月 しがつ, 7月 しちがつ, 9月 くがつ.

questions.question: How to read |今月|?
questions.explanation: 今月 (こんげつ) = this month. Pattern: 今週 こんしゅう, 今月 こんげつ, 今年 ことし (irregular!), 今日 きょう (irregular!).

questions.question: How to read |今年|?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 今年 = ことし (irregular reading). Not こんねん. Famously irregular along with 今日 きょう and 昨日 きのう.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence for: 'I will go to Japan on April 1st.'
choices: 四月一日に日本へ行きます。
四月一日で日本へ行きます。
四月の一日に日本へ行きます。
questions.explanation: Japanese allows both 四月一日に (no の) and 四月の一日に (with の). Both natural. The で option is wrong — に marks point in time.

questions.question: Choose correct: 図書館(___)本を読みます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Particle trap: 図書館 is the LOCATION OF AN ACTION (reading), so で. に would be wrong here — に for location is only used with state verbs like います/あります.

questions.question: Choose correct: 公園(___)子供がいます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Particle trap: with います / あります (existence), use に for location. Compare with w2h-017: action verbs take で, existence verbs take に.

questions.question: Choose correct: 駅(___)友達に会います。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Tricky: 会います takes に for the PERSON met (友達に), but で for the PLACE of meeting. So: 駅で 友達に 会います.

questions.question: Choose correct: 母(___)電話します。
questions.explanation: 電話します takes に for the recipient (the person you call). 母に電話します = call mother. Note: と would mean 'with mother' (collaborative), changing the meaning.

questions.question: Choose correct particle: 鉛筆(___)名前を書きます。
questions.explanation: で marks INSTRUMENT/TOOL: 鉛筆で = with a pencil. Same particle as 'by transport' — both are 'means of doing something'.

questions.question: Choose correct: 日本語(___)話します。
questions.explanation: で marks the LANGUAGE used (a means/method). 日本語で話します = speak IN Japanese. NOT を — を would only work if you're 'speaking the Japanese language' as an object, which is unnatural.

questions.question: Which is most natural? 'I will go to school by walking.'
choices: 歩いて学校へ行きます。
歩いてで学校へ行きます。
歩きで学校へ行きます。
歩くで学校へ行きます。
questions.answer: 歩いて学校へ行きます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 歩いて (on foot) takes NO particle. It's already a verbal form (て-form of 歩く). 歩いてで is wrong because て-form already means 'by means of'.

questions.question: Choose correct: 来週(___)京都へ行きます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 来週 (next week), 先週 (last week), 今週 (this week), 毎週 (every week) take NO particle. Only specific dates/times take に. Same rule as 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日.

questions.question: Choose correct: 月曜日(___)日本へ行きます。
questions.explanation: Days of the week may take に optionally. Both 月曜日に and 月曜日 are natural. (But specific clock times REQUIRE に, and relative time words like 今日/明日/毎日 NEVER take に.)

questions.question: Choose correct: 子供(___)プレゼントをあげます。
questions.explanation: に marks the RECIPIENT of giving (あげます). 子供に プレゼントを あげます = give a present TO a child. を is for the present itself.

questions.question: Choose correct: 七時半(___)朝ごはんを食べます。
questions.explanation: Specific clock times (7時半 = 7:30) ALWAYS require に. Half-hours behave the same as full hours.

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT sentence:
choices: 毎朝に七時に起きます。
questions.answer: 毎朝に七時に起きます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 毎朝 (every morning) takes NO に. Same rule as 毎日/毎晩/毎週. The 七時に inside is fine — clock times require に.

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT sentence:
choices: 友達と映画で見ました。
友達と映画を見ました。
友達と一緒に映画を見ました。
友達と公園で会いました。
questions.answer: 友達と映画で見ました。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Should be 映画を見ました (movie is the OBJECT, takes を). で would only work if 映画 were a location ('at the movies') — but here it's the thing being watched.

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT sentence:
choices: 私はお茶を買いました。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 飲みます is an action verb → uses を, not が. が is for state expressions like 好きです, わかります, あります. So: お茶を飲みます but お茶が好きです.

questions.question: Choose correct: スプーン(___)スープを食べますか?
questions.explanation: ⚠ TWO traps: (1) スプーン is a tool → で, NOT に. (2) In Japanese, soup is DRUNK not eaten: スープを飲みます. Whole correct sentence: スプーンでスープを飲みます.

questions.question: Choose correct: 薬(___)?
questions.explanation: ⚠ Idiom: in Japanese, you DRINK medicine (薬を飲みます), not eat it. Even pills. This is a common N5 trap.

questions.question: Choose correct: タバコ(___)?
questions.explanation: Cigarettes are 'inhaled' (吸います), not drunk. Note: 吸います is N5 vocabulary. Idiom matters more than literal meaning.

questions.question: Translate: 'I do not eat meat at all.'
choices: 私は肉を全然食べません。
私は肉を全然食べました。
私は肉が全然食べません。
私は肉を全然食べます。
questions.answer: 私は肉を全然食べません。
questions.explanation: 全然 (zenzen) pairs with NEGATIVE form. Object 肉 takes を. Present negative habitual = 食べません.

questions.question: Translate: 'Yesterday I did not study Japanese.'
choices: 昨日、日本語を勉強しませんでした。
昨日、日本語を勉強しません。
昨日に、日本語を勉強しませんでした。
昨日、日本語が勉強しませんでした。
questions.answer: 昨日、日本語を勉強しませんでした。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Multiple traps: (1) 昨日 takes NO に. (2) Past negative = ませんでした, not just ません. (3) Object marker is を for action verbs.

questions.question: Translate: 'Tomorrow I am going to my friend's house.' (speaker at own location)
choices: 明日、友達の家へ行きます。
明日、友達の家へ来ます。
明日、友達の家へ帰ります。
明日、友達の家を行きます。
questions.answer: 明日、友達の家へ行きます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ Direction trap: from speaker's perspective (currently at own home), going TO friend's house = 行きます (away from current location). 来ます would mean friend is coming here.

questions.question: On the phone, your friend says: '今晩、私の家に___?' Choose the most natural verb (perspective: from listener's house TO friend's house).
questions.explanation: ⚠ 来ます/行きます depend on PERSPECTIVE OF THE SPEAKER. Friend (asking) is at their house, asking if you'll come TO their location → 来ますか from their viewpoint. English uses 'come' here too.

questions.question: After work, the most natural verb to use for 'going back to your own home' is:
questions.explanation: ⚠ 帰ります specifically means returning to one's HOME or HOMEBASE (家, 国, 会社 if it's your company). 行きます would just be 'go to' — less natural for going home.

questions.question: Choose correct: 先生に質問(___)?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 聞きます has TWO meanings: (1) listen/hear, (2) ASK a question. 質問を聞きます = ask a question. Note: 質問する also works.

questions.question: Choose the most natural: 音楽(___)?
questions.explanation: Music is LISTENED to (聞きます), not seen/read. Different from English which sometimes says 'see a concert'.

questions.question: Choose the most natural verb: テレビ(___)?
questions.explanation: TV is WATCHED (見ます). Even if you only listen, the verb is conventionally 見ます. Compare: ラジオを聞きます (listen to radio).

questions.question: Choose correct: 雑誌(___)?
questions.explanation: 雑誌 (ざっし) = magazine. Magazines are READ (読みます). Note: 見ます (look at) also works for casually flipping through, but 読みます is the standard verb.

questions.question: Translate: 'I went to Tokyo from Osaka by Shinkansen.'
choices: 大阪から東京まで新幹線で行きました。
大阪まで東京から新幹線で行きました。
大阪から東京で新幹線まで行きました。
大阪に東京へ新幹線で行きました。
questions.answer: 大阪から東京まで新幹線で行きました。
questions.explanation: Word order: [start から] [end まで] [means で] [verb]. から = from, まで = until/to, で = means. Past tense 行きました.

questions.question: Translate: 'We worked from 9 in the morning until 6 in the evening.'
choices: 午前九時から午後六時まで働きました。
午前九時まで午後六時から働きました。
九時午前から六時午後まで働きました。
午前九時に午後六時に働きました。
questions.answer: 午前九時から午後六時まで働きました。
questions.explanation: Order: 午前 (AM) before number, then から/まで. 午前 = AM, 午後 = PM. Past = 働きました.

questions.question: Translate the Japanese sentence: 私は毎朝六時半に起きて、七時に朝ごはんを食べます。
choices: I wake up at 6:30 every morning and eat breakfast at 7:00.
I wake up at 7:00 every morning and eat breakfast at 6:30.
Every morning I sleep at 6:30 and wake at 7:00.
I wake up at 6:00 every morning and eat at 7:30.
questions.answer: I wake up at 6:30 every morning and eat breakfast at 7:00.
questions.explanation: 毎朝 = every morning. 六時半 = 6:30. 起きて = wake up (te-form, just for connecting). 七時 = 7:00. 朝ごはん = breakfast.

questions.question: Translate: 来週の土曜日、家族と一緒に山へ行きます。
choices: Next Saturday, I will go to the mountain with my family.
Last Saturday, I went to the mountain with my family.
Every Saturday, I go to the mountain with my family.
Next Saturday, I will go to the mountain alone.
questions.answer: Next Saturday, I will go to the mountain with my family.
questions.explanation: 来週 = next week. 土曜日 = Saturday. 家族と一緒に = together with family. 山へ行きます = go to the mountain (future). NO past markers.

questions.question: Translate: 子供は二人います。一人は男の子で、一人は女の子です。
choices: I have two children. One is a boy, one is a girl.
I have two boys and one girl.
I have one child, a boy and girl.
I have two children, both boys.
questions.answer: I have two children. One is a boy, one is a girl.
questions.explanation: 二人 = two people (here: children). 一人は…一人は… = 'one is..., the other is...'. 男の子 = boy, 女の子 = girl. で connects two clauses.

questions.question: Read: A: 「今日は何曜日ですか?」 B: 「今日は水曜日です。明日は木曜日ですよ。」 What day is the day after tomorrow (明後日)?
questions.explanation: Today = 水曜日 (Wed). Tomorrow = 木曜日 (Thu). Day after tomorrow (明後日 = あさって) = 金曜日 (Fri). Order: 月→火→水→木→金→土→日.

questions.question: Read: 田中さんは毎日朝六時に起きます。でも、土曜日と日曜日は八時に起きます。 On Sunday, what time does Tanaka-san wake up?
questions.explanation: 毎日…六時 (normally 6:00) でも (but) 土曜日と日曜日は八時 (Sat/Sun = 8:00). Sunday is included in the exception.

questions.question: Read: 私はバスで会社へ行きます。会社から家まで電車で帰ります。 What is the means of GOING to work?
questions.explanation: Trap: TWO different transports in one passage. 会社へ行きます = go TO company → バス. 家まで電車で帰ります = return home by train. The question asks about GOING (行きます).

questions.question: Conjugate to past negative: 来ます
questions.explanation: Past negative = ませんでした. So 来ます → 来ませんでした (kimasen deshita) = did not come. Note kanji 来 stays the same; reading is き- here.

questions.question: Conjugate to past affirmative: 帰ります
questions.explanation: Past affirmative = ました. 帰ります → 帰りました = returned home. Reading: かえりました.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjugation: 昨日、私は何も___。 (= 'Yesterday I didn't eat anything.')
questions.explanation: ⚠ TWO clues: 昨日 (yesterday) → past tense; 何も + negative = 'nothing'. Combined: past + negative = 食べませんでした.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjugation: 来週、友達が日本へ___。
questions.explanation: 来週 (next week) → future → present-tense ます form (Japanese has no separate future tense). 来ます (きます) = will come.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjugation: 毎晩十一時に___。
questions.explanation: 毎晩 (every night) signals HABITUAL action → present tense ます. Habitual present is the default for routines.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjugation: 先週の日曜日、私は仕事を___。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 先週の日曜日 = last Sunday → PAST tense. 仕事を休みます = take off work. Past affirmative → 休みました.

questions.question: Choose: お父さんは毎日新聞を___。
questions.explanation: 毎日 → habitual present. 新聞 (newspaper) is READ (読みます). 見ます would also be possible casually but 読みます is more natural.

questions.question: Which sentence has CORRECT grammar?
choices: 私は毎日学校へ電車で行きます。
私は学校へ毎日電車で行きます。
私は電車で毎日学校へ行きます。
All three sentences are grammatically correct.
questions.answer: All three sentences are grammatically correct.
questions.explanation: Japanese is relatively flexible with adverb/time/means order before the verb. All three are grammatical, though option 1 is the most common ordering (Subject-Time-Place-Means-Verb).

questions.question: Which sentence has INCORRECT grammar?
questions.explanation: ⚠ これの本 is unnatural — これ is a standalone pronoun, not used as a noun modifier with の. Use この本 (this book) or これは…の本です.

questions.question: Choose correct: A: 「あの人は___ですか?」 B: 「ベトナム人です。」
questions.explanation: ⚠ Pronunciation matters: here 何人 = なんじん (= 'what nationality?'), NOT なんにん (= 'how many people?'). Same kanji, different reading by context.

questions.question: How many readings does the kanji |日| have? (Match each: 日曜日, 三日, 毎日, 日本)
choices: にち, か, にち, に (4 different uses)
ひ, ひ, ひ, ひ (always ひ)
にち, にち, にち, にち (always にち)
ひ, か, にち, ほん (each different)
questions.answer: にち, か, にち, に (4 different uses)
questions.explanation: 日曜日 にちようび (にち), 三日 みっか (か), 毎日 まいにち (にち), 日本 にほん (に — irregular). 日 has many context-dependent readings — one of the most variable kanji.

questions.question: How is |月| read in: 月曜日 / 一月 / 月見?
choices: げつ / がつ / つき
げつ / げつ / げつ
つき / つき / つき
がつ / がつ / がつ
questions.answer: げつ / がつ / つき
questions.explanation: 月曜日 げつようび (げつ), 一月 いちがつ (がつ for month names), 月見 つきみ (moon-viewing, kun-yomi つき). Three different on/kun depending on compound.

questions.question: Read this: 火曜日の午後三時に山田さんと駅で会います。 What is the meeting POINT?
questions.explanation: Question asks for the LOCATION (point of meeting). 駅で = at the station. 火曜日午後三時 = time, 山田さん = person met (with に).

questions.question: Translate the Japanese: 来月の十日に、家族と一緒に京都の山へ行きます。
choices: On the 10th of next month, I will go to the mountains in Kyoto with my family.
Last month on the 10th, I went to the mountains in Kyoto with my family.
On the 10th of this month, I am going to Kyoto by myself.
Next month, I will go to Kyoto on the 10th by mountain train.
questions.answer: On the 10th of next month, I will go to the mountains in Kyoto with my family.
questions.explanation: 来月 = next month. 十日 (とおか) = 10th. 家族と一緒に = with family. 京都の山 = mountains of Kyoto. 行きます = will go.

questions.question: Read: 田中さんは火曜日と木曜日の朝、日本語を勉強します。今日は水曜日です。明日、田中さんは日本語を勉強しますか?
choices: いいえ、勉強しませんでした。
questions.explanation: Tanaka studies on 火 (Tue) and 木 (Thu). Today = 水 (Wed) → tomorrow = 木 (Thu) → YES, studies. Future/habitual → 勉強します.

questions.question: Read: 私は毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。でも、今朝は紅茶を飲みました。 What did I drink THIS morning?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 毎朝 (every morning) = coffee USUALLY. でも (but) 今朝 (this morning) = 紅茶 (tea). Trap: don't pick the habitual answer; the question asks about THIS specific morning.

questions.question: What does |今朝| mean and how is it read?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 今朝 has IRREGULAR reading けさ (NOT こんあさ). Means 'this morning' specifically. Compare: 毎朝 まいあさ (every morning), 朝 あさ (morning).

questions.question: What does |今晩| mean and how is it read?
questions.explanation: 今晩 (こんばん) = tonight. Common phrase: 今晩は (こんばんは, written 今晩は) = good evening.

questions.question: Order the words to form a correct sentence: [食べました] [パンを] [私は] [今朝]
choices: 私は今朝パンを食べました。
私は食べましたパンを今朝。
今朝パンを私は食べました。
私はパンを食べました今朝。
questions.answer: 私は今朝パンを食べました。
questions.explanation: Standard order: [Topic は] [Time] [Object を] [Verb]. 私は (topic) → 今朝 (time) → パンを (object) → 食べました (verb).

questions.question: Order the words: [行きません] [日曜日] [会社へ] [は]
choices: 日曜日は会社へ行きません。
会社へ日曜日は行きません。
日曜日会社へは行きません。
会社へは日曜日行きません。
questions.answer: 日曜日は会社へ行きません。
questions.explanation: は after 日曜日 makes 'as for Sunday' the topic (contrast: 'on Sunday specifically'). Standard: Topic-Time → Place → Verb. 日曜日は会社へ行きません = 'On Sunday I don't go to the company.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'I will not go to school this Saturday.'
choices: 今週の土曜日、学校へ行きません。
今週の土曜日、学校に行きません。
今週土曜日、学校で行きません。
questions.explanation: Both へ and に work for direction of movement (school as destination). へ slightly emphasizes direction; に is more neutral. The で option is wrong (で is for action location).

questions.question: What is the most natural reading of |二人| in: 二人で映画を見ました?
questions.explanation: 二人 = ふたり regardless of context. 二人で = '(just) the two of us'. Common phrase: 二人で食事する = eat as a couple/pair.

questions.question: Choose correct: A: 「いくらですか?」 B: 「___です。」 Choose what fills the blank for '3500 yen':
questions.explanation: 3500 yen = 三千 (3000) + 五百 (500) + 円. Note: in Japanese, prices are read as full place-value numbers — say 三千五百円 (sanzen gohyaku en).

questions.question: How to read |三千五百円|?
choices: さんぜんごひゃくえん
さんせんごひゃくえん
さんぜんごひゃくいぇん
みっせんごひゃくえん
questions.answer: さんぜんごひゃくえん
questions.explanation: ⚠ Sound change: 千 alone is せん, but 三千 = さんぜん (sequential voicing). 5000 = ごせん (no voicing). Memorize: 1千 せん, 2千 にせん, 3千 さんぜん, 8千 はっせん.

questions.question: How to read |八千|?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 八千 = はっせん (sound change). Pattern of 千 readings: 1=せん, 2=にせん, 3=さんぜん (voiced), 8=はっせん (small tsu).

questions.question: How to read |一万円|?
questions.explanation: 10,000 yen = 一万円 (いちまんえん). ⚠ Note: in Japanese, must say 一万 (ichi-man), NOT just 万 (man) — unlike how English just says 'ten thousand'.

questions.question: Translate: 'How much is one of these?' (pointing at items)
choices: これは一ついくらですか。
これは一いくらですか。
questions.answer: これは一ついくらですか。
questions.explanation: 一つ (ひとつ) = one item (general counter). 一ついくら = 'how much per one'. いくつ would mean 'how many'.

questions.question: Translate: '500 yen for two.'
questions.explanation: Pattern: [counter]で[price] = 'for [counter], price is...'. 二つで五百円 = 'for two, 500 yen' (i.e., 2 items cost 500 yen total).

questions.question: Read: A: 「映画は何時に始まりますか?」 B: 「七時半に始まります。」 What time does the movie start?
questions.explanation: 七時半 = 7:30 (七時 7 o'clock + 半 half). 始まります (はじまります) = begin/start. に marks the time.

questions.question: Translate: 学校は八時半に始まって、三時半に終わります。
choices: School starts at 8:30 and ends at 3:30.
School starts at 3:30 and ends at 8:30.
School is half past 8 and half past 3.
questions.answer: School starts at 8:30 and ends at 3:30.
questions.explanation: 始まる (begin) and 終わる (end). 八時半 8:30 → 三時半 3:30. The て-form connects two related clauses ('starts at X and ends at Y').

questions.question: Choose correct: A: 「明日、何をしますか?」 B: 「___」
choices: 友達と買い物に行きます。
友達と買い物で行きます。
友達と買い物を行きます。
友達は買い物に行きます。
questions.answer: 友達と買い物に行きます。
questions.explanation: に行きます is used for purpose of going (to go FOR shopping). 買い物に行く = go shopping. と marks 'with friend'.

questions.question: Find the natural meaning: 私は毎晩、家でテレビを見て、本を読んで、寝ます。
choices: Every night I watch TV at home, read a book, and (then) sleep.
Every night I sleep while watching TV and reading.
Tonight I will watch TV and read.
I watch TV in bed every night.
questions.answer: Every night I watch TV at home, read a book, and (then) sleep.
questions.explanation: 毎晩 (every night), 家で (at home — action location → で). The te-form 見て / 読んで chains actions in sequence: 'watch TV, read, then sleep.'

questions.question: What does |誰と| ask?
questions.explanation: 誰 (だれ) = who. 誰と = with whom (と marks 'together with'). Compare: 誰が = who (subject), 誰に = to whom.

questions.question: How to read |何曜日|?
questions.explanation: 何 has two readings なん/なに. Before counters or つ-words it's なん: 何時 なんじ, 何人 なんにん/なんじん, 何曜日 なんようび. Before vowels often なに: 何が, 何を.

questions.question: Translate: 駅から学校までバスで二十分かかります。
choices: From the station to school, it takes 20 minutes by bus.
It takes 20 minutes from the school to the station.
I walk 20 minutes from station to school.
The bus takes 20 yen from station to school.
questions.answer: From the station to school, it takes 20 minutes by bus.
questions.explanation: から…まで = from…to. 二十分 (にじゅっぷん) = 20 minutes. かかります = takes (time/cost). バスで = by bus.

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT sentence:
choices: 昨日に映画を見ました。
昨日、友達と映画を見ました。
questions.answer: 昨日に映画を見ました。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 昨日 (yesterday) takes NO に. Same as 今日, 明日, 毎日. The 4th option is also unnatural word order, but the 1st has a clear grammar error (overuse of に).

questions.question: Find the most NATURAL Japanese sentence for 'My father is a teacher.'
choices: 私の父は先生がいます。
questions.explanation: When talking about your OWN family humbly, 父 (chichi) alone is fine — 私の is often dropped because context makes it clear. Both versions work.

questions.question: Read: A: 「日本へ何で来ましたか?」 B: 「飛行機で来ました。」 What does 何で mean here?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 何で (なんで) ambiguity: can mean 'why' OR 'by what means' depending on context. Here B answers with a transport (飛行機で = by airplane), so 何で = 'by what means'. For 'why', どうして is clearer.

questions.question: How to read |人| in: あの人?
questions.explanation: ⚠ 人 readings: ひと (kun, when standalone or with の: あの人 ano-hito), じん (in nationality compounds: 日本人), にん (counter: 三人 sannin).

questions.question: Translate: あそこにいる人は誰ですか?
choices: Who is the person over there?
questions.answer: Who is the person over there?
questions.explanation: あそこに = over there (location with いる/います). 人 = person. 誰 = who. Full: 'Who is the person (who is) over there?'

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT use of particles:
choices: 毎日に新聞を読みます。
毎日、家で新聞を読みます。
毎日新聞は読みません。
questions.answer: 毎日に新聞を読みます。
questions.explanation: ⚠ 毎日 NEVER takes に. Memorize the 'no-に time words': 今日, 昨日, 明日, 毎日, 毎朝, 毎晩, 毎週, 毎月, 毎年, 今, いつ.

questions.question: Choose what makes a correct sentence: 大学___九時___始まります。
questions.explanation: 大学は (topic: 'as for university') + 九時に (specific time). 'University starts at 9:00.' The verb 始まります is intransitive — no を.

questions.question: Choose what makes a correct sentence: 私___毎朝___お茶___飲みます。
questions.explanation: 私は (topic) + 毎朝 (NO に — relative time) + お茶を (object) + 飲みます. Three slots, three different particles (or absence).

questions.question: Choose the MOST NATURAL: At a restaurant, you want to order tea. Say:
questions.explanation: ください = please give. お茶をください is the standard polite ordering phrase. 飲みたいです (want to drink) is grammatical but less natural for ordering. ください is N5-essential.

questions.question: Read: 山田さんは去年日本へ来ました。今、東京の大学で日本語を勉強しています。 Where is Yamada-san now?
questions.explanation: 去年 (last year) = came to Japan. 今 (now) = STUDYING at 東京の大学 (Tokyo University). Use the 今 (now) marker to identify the present location.

questions.question: Read: 私の家から駅まで歩いて十五分です。駅から会社まで電車で三十分かかります。 How long is the TOTAL commute from home to office?
questions.explanation: 家→駅 = walk 15 min. 駅→会社 = train 30 min. Total = 15 + 30 = 45 minutes. Trap: don't just pick one of the listed numbers.

questions.question: Read: スミスさんはアメリカ人です。日本語と中国語を話します。英語も話します。スミスさんは何ヶ国語を話しますか?
questions.explanation: Smith speaks: 日本語 (Japanese), 中国語 (Chinese), and 英語 (English) too (も = also). Total = 3 languages. American means English is native — included by も.

questions.question: Read: 木村さんは火曜日の朝、山へ行きました。水曜日の夕方、家へ帰りました。木村さんは山に何日いましたか?
questions.explanation: Went Tue morning, returned Wed evening = spent Tue and Wed = 二日 (ふつか, 2 days). Counted as how many days were involved, not 24-hour periods.

questions.question: Translate: 私の会社は月曜日から金曜日まで仕事があります。土曜日と日曜日は休みです。
choices: At my company, we work Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are off.
I work weekends at my company.
My company is closed Monday to Friday.
I have meetings Monday and Friday only.
questions.answer: At my company, we work Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are off.
questions.explanation: 月曜日から金曜日まで = Mon to Fri. 仕事があります = (we) have work. 休み = day off, holiday. Standard 5-day workweek description.

questions.question: Final challenge — read: 先週の土曜日、私は朝七時に起きて、九時に友達と駅で会いました。それから新幹線で京都へ行きました。京都で四時間お寺を見て、夜八時に東京の家へ帰りました。 What time did I return home?
questions.explanation: Multi-fact reading: 朝七時 (woke up), 九時 (met friend), 四時間 (4 hours sightseeing), 夜八時 (returned home at 8 PM). The question targets 帰りました time → 八時.
